newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close higher, helped by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close higher, helped by Wall Street.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Friday after Wall Street's rebound from yesterday's sell-off triggered a spate of bargain-hunting by foreign and domestic investors.
The all-share Mibtel index finished 0.62 percent higher at 11,955 with the Mib30 blue chip index closing 0.74 percent up at 17,687.

Traders said a rush of late buying drove up Telecom Italia shares to close 3.41 percent higher at 4,394 lire while Stet ended 2.0 percent up at 7,784 lire ahead of an expected announcement of share swap terms for their planned merger.
The ratio between the Stet and Telecom closing prices was in line with market expectations at 1.76.
Brokers also said they were expecting Telecom to announce good 1996 results. "People are expecting good numbers from Telecom Italia tonight," said one broker based in Milan.
After the market closed Telecom Italia announced it posted 1996 net profit of 2.119 trillion lire, up 53.7 percent on 1995, with increased dividends.

Television and advertising group Mediaset ended the day 0.28 percent up at 7,072 lire with investors apparently unruffled by the announcement by Silvio Berlusconi, who controls the group through his Fininvest holding company, that Mediaset would not bid for a mobile phone licence in Italy.
Shares in Unicem surged on rumours that key shareholder Ifil might sell its stake. Bulgari shares advanced after yesterday's announcement of a share split.
Overall trading volumes were forecast as modest at 757 billion lire, down from 789.5 billion on Thursday.
